findings.mechanism: Static HashMap ORDERS_BY_ID gets every new order via store() (line 122) and nothing ever removes entries: no eviction, TTL or size bound. Only invalidateAll(), used by tests, clears it. Each entry keeps the Order with its Line list and notes string reachable forever.
findings.cause: Unbounded idempotency/replay cache keyed by order id (customer + requestId); every distinct request adds a permanent entry.
findings.evidence: Ran shop.Main with 200000 requests; after System.gc() the heap in use grew linearly with cached orders: 26362 KB (43750 orders), 50511 KB (87500), 76280 KB (131250), 100512 KB (175000), about 0.58 KB per order. The cache size equals the number of placed orders.
findings.discriminator: Fix: bound the cache with LRU/TTL eviction (for example a LinkedHashMap with removeEldestEntry or Caffeine), and drop the notes string or store only what a replay needs.

findings.mechanism: The placed and replayed fields are plain int counters, not collections.
findings.cause: Looked at as a possible growth source and ruled out.
findings.evidence: Code inspection. The heap growth in the 200000-request run is fully accounted for by the OrderCache entries.
findings.discriminator: The counters are primitives of constant size. The retry path (every eighth request) hits the cache and allocates no new entry: 25000 replayed requests added 0 orders.
